run.question:
payment-service is throwing 500 errors — investigate the root cause using
the app-263-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The index named in the request, app-263-prod-logs, exists (green) but contains only 7 documents inside the authorized window (2026-11-20T06:07:26Z–2026-11-21T06:07:26Z), and none of them carries the exact service name 'payment-service': the service field has only payment-service-us (3 docs), payment-service-eu (2) and payment-service-ap (2). The errors split into two unrelated regional clusters — payment-service-us reports a 30s upstream timeout to stripe-us, connection-pool exhaustion (max=50, active=50) and a retry queue depth of 812, while payment-service-eu reports an adyen-eu 503 and then 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' — and payment-service-ap reports itself healthy (p95 290ms). No document records an HTTP status code or a 500, so the reported 500s are not directly observable here, and Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) for every query in this run, so error rate, latency and span status could not be checked. In the reachable cluster (otel-demo) the payment workload is Deployment/Service 'payment', not 'payment-service'; it processed charges successfully throughout the sampled hours and checkout logged 'payment went through' continuously, so no failure of that workload was observed. Its container restart at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z was part of a cluster-wide restart of all 33 pods in all namespaces (exit 255, reason Unknown) on a node that never left Ready, so the restart is a mechanism, not a payment-specific fault. No single object can be named as the origin of the reported 500s from this evidence; the candidates remain hypotheses and the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: The app-263-prod-logs index exists (health green) and a search over the whole authorized window on its date field timestamp returned exactly 7 documents (total relation eq, incomplete false) with timestamps 2026-11-21T04:07:17Z, 2026-11-21T05:07:17Z and 2026-11-21T05:37:17Z; the level aggregation over those documents is ERROR=4, INFO=2, WARN=1.

No document in app-263-prod-logs has service exactly 'payment-service'; the service terms aggregation returned only three values: payment-service-us (3 documents), payment-service-ap (2) and payment-service-eu (2).

payment-service-us wrote: ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' at 2026-11-21T04:07:17Z, ERROR 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' at 2026-11-21T05:07:17Z, and WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' at 2026-11-21T05:37:17Z.
payment-service-eu wrote: ERROR 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' at 2026-11-21T04:07:17Z and ERROR 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' at 2026-11-21T05:07:17Z.
payment-service-ap wrote only INFO lines: 'Healthy: p95 latency 290ms' at 2026-11-21T04:07:17Z and 'Healthy' at 2026-11-21T05:37:17Z.
None of the 7 returned app-263-prod-logs documents contains an HTTP status code or the literal '500'; the reported 500 responses are therefore not directly evidenced by this index.

In cluster otel-demo the workload is Deployment and Service 'payment' (selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment, port 8080), served by pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, which is Running and Ready with restartCount 1; its container last terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255 and reason Unknown and restarted at 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z, and it is owned by the single ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6 created 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z.

The payment container's own logs show successful charges: the previous container logged 'Charge request received' followed by 'Transaction complete' up to 2026-11-21T04:07:21Z, and the current container logged the same INFO pairs from 2026-11-21T04:25:26Z through 2026-11-21T06:07:04Z; the only non-INFO line observed after the restart was '(node:24) MetadataLookupWarning: received unexpected error = Invalid response from metadata service: incorrect Metadata-Flavor header' at 2026-11-21T04:23:52Z.

The checkout pod's logs record 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' continuously from 2026-11-21T05:22:59Z to 2026-11-21T06:07:04Z (80 newest of 103 matching lines shown), so no failing payment call is visible from its caller in that window.

A single global payment-service outage is not supported: one of the three app-263 service labels (payment-service-ap) reported healthy with p95 latency 290ms and 'Healthy', and in otel-demo the payment workload completed charges while checkout logged successful payments throughout the last sampled hour.

The payment container's 04:23:42Z termination was part of a cluster-wide event: all 33 pods in app-101, kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo show a container termination at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255 and lastTerm 'Unknown' (a few terminate later with exit 1 or 2), while the single node opspilot-m1-control-plane has had Ready=True with lastTransitionTime 2026-11-20T16:32:02Z and no condition change at 04:23.

The fault-injection settings read in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config have every flag's defaultVariant set to 'off', including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), and the payment Deployment's env contains only PAYMENT_PORT, FLAGD_HOST, FLAGD_PORT and OTEL_* entries with no fault-injection variable; this is the state at query time, not proven for the whole window.

Among the 25 Deployments cluster-wide, the only one whose name matches 'payment' or '263' is otel-demo/payment; namespace app-101 currently holds only Deployment loki, while its events separately record Deployment app-101/payment-api-101 scaling up and pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-v4v9b being Created then Killing between 2026-11-21T05:28Z and 06:06Z, a different entity from the services in app-263-prod-logs.

For payment-service-us the deepest cause the messages support is the external dependency stripe-us not answering within 30s ('Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms'), with 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' and 'Retry queue depth=812' as consequences that would surface as 5xx; no telemetry for stripe-us exists in the reachable data, so this dependency could not be inspected.

For payment-service-eu one candidate cause is a credential/configuration fault: 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' is an exact authentication failure, but the credential value itself is unreadable (secrets are not accessible) and no object holding it is visible, so this cannot be confirmed.

An alternative or additional cause for payment-service-eu is upstream unavailability: 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' at 2026-11-21T04:07:17Z; nothing in the evidence shows whether adyen-eu recovered or whether this 503 and the later api_key error share one cause.

The payment pod container restart at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z is rejected as a payment-specific cause of the reported 500s: the same-second termination with exitCode 255 and lastTerm 'Unknown' occurred for all 33 pods in every namespace, the node never left Ready, the pod template is unchanged (single ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6 created 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z), and payment resumed successful charges at 04:25:26Z with checkout logging 'payment went through' through 06:07:04Z.

gaps: Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query in this run (get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, list_prometheus_rules, traces_list_services, traces_search), so error rate, latency and span status for any payment service could not be measured and the claimed 500 responses could not be verified, counted or timed.

app-263-prod-logs contains only 7 documents and no document with service exactly 'payment-service', so which regional service the report refers to is unknown, and the limited sample cannot show when errors started or whether they persist.
No telemetry exists in the reachable data for the upstream dependencies named in the messages (stripe-us, adyen-eu); their health at 04:07–05:07Z is unknown.
The adyen-eu API key value could not be read (secrets are not readable), so the authentication-failure cause cannot be confirmed or corrected from evidence.

The trigger of the cluster-wide container restart at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z was not identified: no events for those pods were recorded in the authorized window (only app-101 Deployment/Pod events were returned) and the node's Ready condition has not changed since 2026-11-20T16:32:02Z.
The flagd defaultVariant values were read at query time only; whether any injection flag was on during 04:07–05:37Z is unknown, and flagd produced no log lines for the queried window (0 lines read).
Log history is incomplete: the previous instances of the checkout and flagd containers returned 0 log lines, so pre-restart behaviour of the caller is unknown.
Change history is not an integrated data source in this run, so configuration and credential changes around the error timestamps cannot be reviewed.
A cluster-wide ConfigMap name search for '263|payment-service|adyen|stripe' returned nothing with view status no_data, so it establishes nothing about the absence of such objects.
next_steps: Determine which regional payment service instance (payment-service-us, payment-service-eu or payment-service-ap) the report concerns and obtain the alert or load-balancer evidence showing the actual 5xx responses and their onset time.
Have a human with secret access validate the adyen-eu API key/credential used by payment-service-eu and check whether it was rotated near 2026-11-21T05:07Z.
Check stripe-us latency and error metrics from its own monitoring, and review payment-service-us connection-pool sizing (max=50) against its 30s upstream timeout.
Restore or repair the Prometheus and Jaeger integrations so traces_span_metrics_calls_total status_code and span error data for the payment service can be queried.
Review change history for payment-service configurations and credentials between 2026-11-21T04:00Z and 2026-11-21T05:40Z.
Establish why all containers in all namespaces restarted at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (container runtime restart on the kind node) even though the restart is not the cause of the reported payment errors.
